soru: Dil modellerinin iç aktivasyonlarını yorumlanabilir özelliklere ayıran seyrek otokodlayıcı yöntemleri üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, değerlendirme yaklaşımları ve açık problemler neler?
istem:
Research question: Dil modellerinin iç aktivasyonlarını yorumlanabilir özelliklere ayıran seyrek otokodlayıcı yöntemleri üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, değerlendirme yaklaşımları ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2026-09-14. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
calismalar.gerekce: Anthropic's foundational work, published on transformer-circuits.pub, which showed that dictionary learning with SAEs splits polysemantic neurons into monosemantic features.

calismalar.baslik: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: First peer-reviewed (ICLR 2024) work to show that SAEs find features in LLM activations that are more interpretable than alternative methods and can be causally localized.

calismalar.baslik: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
calismalar.gerekce: Scaled SAEs to a production model (Claude 3 Sonnet), extracting millions of abstract, multilingual and safety-relevant features and demonstrating steering.

calismalar.baslik: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced TopK SAEs, scaling laws and new quality metrics, and trained a 16-million-latent SAE on GPT-4.

calismalar.baslik: Toy Models of Superposition
calismalar.gerekce: Set out the theoretical basis of the superposition hypothesis, which motivates the SAE approach.

calismalar.baslik: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
calismalar.gerekce: Released more than 2,000 open JumpReLU SAEs covering every layer of Gemma 2, which became standard infrastructure for the research community.

calismalar.baslik: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Proposed the JumpReLU architecture, which uses learned thresholds and direct L0 training to reach state-of-the-art reconstruction-sparsity trade-offs.

calismalar.baslik: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Separated feature selection from magnitude estimation to address the L1 shrinkage problem, a major architectural improvement.

calismalar.baslik: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that SAE features can be used for causal circuit discovery and downstream editing (SHIFT).

calismalar.baslik: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
calismalar.gerekce: Standardized SAE evaluation with eight metrics and showed that proxy metrics do not reliably predict practical performance.

calismalar.baslik: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
calismalar.gerekce: Proposed transcoders, a sparse dictionary variant that makes circuit analysis through MLP layers tractable.

calismalar.baslik: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Released an open-source pipeline and new scoring methods for automatically interpreting SAE features at scale.

calismalar.baslik: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Defined and measured feature absorption, a basic failure mode that arises from optimizing for sparsity when features are hierarchical.

calismalar.baslik: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
calismalar.gerekce: A key critical evaluation finding that SAEs do not consistently beat strong baselines on probing tasks.

calismalar.baslik: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Benchmark showing that SAEs fall behind simple methods such as prompting and difference-in-means for steering and concept detection.

calismalar.baslik: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
calismalar.gerekce: Used SAE stitching and meta-SAEs to show that SAE features are not canonical units, an open problem that depends on dictionary size.

calismalar.baslik: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
calismalar.gerekce: Broad overview that systematically lays out the conceptual and practical limits and open problems of SAE-based decomposition.

calismalar.baslik: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
calismalar.gerekce: Trained SAEs with a KL objective on model outputs rather than reconstruction to find functionally important features.

calismalar.baslik: Towards Principled Evaluations of Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability and Control
calismalar.gerekce: Proposed principled evaluation by comparing SAEs against supervised feature dictionaries on a task with known concepts (IOI).

calismalar.baslik: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Moved the TopK constraint to the batch level, allowing adaptive sparsity per sample and improving performance.

calismalar.baslik: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Used nested dictionaries to learn hierarchical features and substantially reduce absorption and feature splitting.

calismalar.baslik: Sparse Crosscoders for Cross-Layer Features and Model Diffing
calismalar.gerekce: Extended SAEs to cross-layer features and to model diffing, i.e. comparing two models.

calismalar.baslik: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Built attribution graphs from cross-layer transcoders, the most comprehensive application of sparse dictionaries to circuit analysis.

calismalar.baslik: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Released 256 TopK SAEs covering every layer of Llama-3.1-8B and studied how they generalize to longer contexts and fine-tuned models.

calismalar.baslik: Transcoders Beat Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that transcoder features are more interpretable than SAE features and introduced skip transcoders.

calismalar.baslik: Sparse Autoencoders Can Interpret Randomly Initialized Transformers
calismalar.gerekce: Showed that SAEs on random models get similar auto-interpretability scores, exposing a serious validity problem in evaluation metrics.

calismalar.baslik: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Analyzed SAE reconstruction error ('dark matter') and separated it into linearly predictable and nonlinear parts.

calismalar.baslik: Language models can explain neurons in language models
calismalar.gerekce: Introduced the explanation-and-simulation-scoring automated interpretability method that became the basis for evaluating SAE features.

calismalar.baslik: A Survey on Sparse Autoencoders: Interpreting the Internal Mechanisms of Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Comprehensive survey of SAE architectures, explanation methods, evaluation metrics and applications (EMNLP 2025 Findings).

calismalar.baslik: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
calismalar.gerekce: Extended SAEs to attention layer outputs, making attention mechanisms interpretable through features.
